ideas.pitch: A multi-agent auditing system that checks automated insurance or financial decisions for discriminatory bias and policy compliance.
ideas.title: ClaimAudit AI
ideas.why_it_could_win: Directly targets the Technical Implementation and Problem Solving judging criteria by incorporating complex multi-agent reasoning, directly inspired by a Google Code Cure Hackathon winner.

ideas.pitch: An optimized mobile-first CNN classifier for early plant disease detection designed for low-bandwidth rural deployments.
ideas.title: AgriGuard Mobile
ideas.why_it_could_win: Features clear measurable impact and practical execution by focusing on optimized inference times, following the pattern of a CONIA Hackathon winner.

ideas.pitch: An AI-powered smart recycling classification pipeline utilizing computer vision and hardware simulation models.
ideas.title: EcoSort Edge
ideas.why_it_could_win: High marks for Functionality and UI/UX with a live-working webcam demo, mirroring the runner-up success at the TechnoMorph Hackathon.

ideas.pitch: A localized voice and text AI assistant providing instant preventive health guidance and symptom tracking in regional languages.
ideas.title: RuralMed Multilingual
ideas.why_it_could_win: Addresses social impact directly and secures high presentation points through a fully functional localized demo, drawing from the First Prize Hackathon winner.

ideas.pitch: A geospatial predictive data model estimating regional wildfire risk intervals using environmental datasets and Poisson regression.
ideas.title: WildfireRisk Simulator
ideas.why_it_could_win: Leverages heavy data science implementation and statistical rigor to impress judges on Technical Implementation, based on the Sacramento State AI Hackathon winner.
